extracted.intended_audience: Anyone who wishes to communicate well in writing (general writers, students, editors, and professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: A general-purpose guide to clear, concise, and effective writing covering word usage, grammar, punctuation, tone and style, and narrative/structural components for fiction and nonfiction. Intended to help writers decide which conventional 'rules' to follow or set aside based on purpose and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, concise, effective writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear, concise, effective — THE RANDOM HOUSE GUIDE TO GOOD WRITING is for anyone who wishes to communicate well in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes clarity, concision, and effectiveness as overarching goals for writing; the book teaches how to 'master the medium and the message' to achieve these qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master the medium and the message
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitchell Ivers shows us how to master the medium and the message with an array of features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats both the technical form (medium) and the communicative content (message) as aspects writers must control; practical features aim to align form and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise guidelines on word usage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers concrete advice on choosing the right words for meaning and tone; part of a trio with grammar and punctuation to improve sentence-level clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides rules and explanations of grammatical usage to ensure correctness and clarity in prose; also discusses when traditional grammatical rules may be set aside to suit purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers punctuation conventions to aid readability and meaning, while acknowledging choices writers can make about which punctuation 'rules' to follow or discard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deciding which rules to discard to suit purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: …and how to decide with "rules" you can discard to suit your purpose;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all conventional rules are absolute; provides guidance for deliberate departures from rules based on audience, tone, and rhetorical effect—i.e., purposeful rule-breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing tone and style appropriate to audience and subject
rubrics_metrics.description: How to choose the tone and style appropriate to your audience and subject;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps writers match tone (formal/informal, intimate/impersonal, etc.) and stylistic choices to the intended audience and subject matter; includes criteria for making those decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential components of plot in fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential components of plot in fiction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies and explains core plot elements fiction writers should include and develop (structure, conflict, pacing, resolution) to craft effective narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure in nonfiction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers organizing principles for nonfiction (logical structure, sequencing, exposition, signposting) so arguments and information are presented clearly and persuasively.
